# GSQ224 complete Engine coding pilot

GSQ224 accepts 53 of 56 drafts and needs 28 target passes instead of 81. Observed target expert traffic remains about 32.94 versus 32.91 GB because cache/routing behavior differs, despite smaller records. I/O and verify counters overlap and are not a causal wall-time decomposition. The result supports a useful complete-configuration route; it does not isolate quantization benefit.

Next use one equally bounded original forced-streamed-two-draft coding pilot, if the honest ten-GB planner admits it, before attributing the gain to the pack. Then confirm genuinely better configurations on the existing short/context/coding workloads with a few paired rounds, preserving quality, complete-request latency and physical memory.
